ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram there is an operational amplifier. The non-inverting input terminal (+) is connected to a voltage source labeled 10 V, whose negative terminal is grounded. The node where the inverting input terminal (−) is located is grounded through a 1 kΩ resistor. This inverting input node is also connected through switch S to the left end of a capacitor labeled C = 1 μF; the right end of the capacitor is connected to the op-amp output terminal vo. The polarity of the capacitor voltage Vc is marked in the figure as left end − and right end +, that is, the positive terminal is on the output side. The problem states that the capacitor is initially uncharged, switch S closes at t = 0, and asks for Vc at t = 1 ms. Reasoning: According to the specified method, before the switch closes, because V+ = 10 V and V− is approximately 0 V, the op-amp output is regarded as positively saturated, and an implied positive supply rail of about 15 V is adopted. After the switch closes, regard the capacitor as charging toward 15 V through the 1 kΩ resistor, with time constant τ = RC = (1 kΩ)(1 μF) = 1 ms. The capacitor voltage is Vc(t) = 15(1 − e^(−t/τ)). At t = 1 ms, t/τ = 1, so Vc = 15(1 − e^(−1)) ≈ 9.45 V.
